item.description:
### The Assistant can do what it suggests
- **Approve, and it's done.** When an answer suggests quitting idle apps, shutting down a simulator, a Careful clean, restarting a leaking macOS helper such as the Wi-Fi menu, or a speed test, a card under the answer lists each one with **Approve** and **Not Now**. A clean it ran has **Put Back**, and after a speed test the Assistant tells you what the result means. - **Choose how much it does by itself.** Settings › Assistant › Actions, also at the bottom of the conversation: **Ask Every Time** (the default) waits for you; **Auto** has a second AI check each action and runs it if that AI approves; **Full Access** runs them straight away. - **Glade's rules still decide.** Only what Free Up Memory or the clean level would choose, or what you named, ever runs by itself. Personal files, anything permanent and a speed test on a metered connection always wait for you, and the second AI can stop an action but never allow one. In Auto or Full Access, an app you asked to uninstall goes to the Trash without the extra confirmation, one at a time.
### Uninstall any app
- Apps that belong to the system, which includes most from the App Store such as iMovie, Keynote and Xcode, can now be uninstalled from Glade like any other. Glade asks Finder to move the app, and Finder asks for your password or Touch ID; Glade never sees it. The first time, macOS asks whether Glade may control Finder. **Put Back** brings the app back the same way. - The Assistant can now propose these apps when you name them, ticked like the rest. - On the command line, `glade uninstall --finder` and `glade undo --finder` do the same.
### Assistant
- **Your conversations are kept.** A column beside the conversation lists earlier ones under Pinned, Today, Yesterday and so on. Open any to read it or carry on, and rename, pin or delete it from its menu. Starting a new conversation no longer loses the last one. - **Questions go where you meant.** A pasted screenshot's file name no longer turns a question into a clean-up ("CleanShot" isn't "clean"), and a follow-up in a conversation about your network still gets your network's readings. - **It knows what Glade can do with your router.** The Assistant is told whether your gateway's access code is saved, so it no longer says it can't see it or sends you to the sticker. - **Effort for each AI.** Choose how hard each AI thinks, and the second opinion too, in Settings › Assistant or under the question box. - **Signing in to an AI is one click.** An AI that needs signing in, such as Gemini, has **Sign In…**, which opens Terminal running its command, and a button to copy the command. Glade looks again when you come back. - **Links in answers open.** A web address in an answer can be clicked.
### Performance and Network
- **Unfamiliar names explain themselves.** `swift-frontend` says it's the Swift compiler, `node` says it's JavaScript and which app started it, and macOS helpers that leak, such as the Wi-Fi menu, are marked when they use far more memory than usual. - **Forget removes your router's access code.** It did nothing when a different copy of Glade had saved the code; now it removes it, or says why it couldn't. - **Little Snitch's import date and Import Again… sit together** at the top of its card.
### Fixed
- An app you deleted by hand but installed with Homebrew no longer keeps its leftovers hidden from App Leftovers.

- **Adding your AT&T gateway's access code works.** Saving the Device Access Code always said "The router didn't answer", even on the router's own network. Glade now signs in and keeps the code in your Keychain, and if the router really is slow to answer, it says so instead of claiming it can't sign in to that router. - **The Assistant's answers line up with the question box.** Answers start where your typing does, and buttons such as **Save Cleaned Backup…**, **Copy** and **Show What Was Sent** sit on the same edge as the answer's text.

### Network
- A new **Network** section answers "is it my Wi-Fi, my internet, or the service?" It draws your connection from this Mac to your router, your provider and the internet, each with its latency, so a slow hop stands out, and leads with a plain verdict such as "Uploads are making everything wait" or "Your Wi-Fi signal is weak here". - **Latency** updates every second while the section is open, like the ping graph in a call app. **Wi-Fi** shows the signal, band, channel and link rate. - **Test Speed** runs macOS's own speed test when you ask. It tells you first how much data it will use, then how much slower your line gets when it's busy, and whether that's good enough for calls, 4K and game streaming. - **Using the Network** lists the apps sending and receiving the most, now and today, and Performance gains a Network column. - **Data Used** counts what this Mac used today, this week and this month, by day, app and network, while Glade is open. - To tell your networks apart by name, macOS asks for Location access the first time. Everything else works without it. - **Settings > Network** turns the section off, changes the host latency is measured against, and sets how long a speed test runs.
### Your router
- On an AT&T gateway, **Your Network** shows whether your internet line is up and lists the devices on your network with their signal, without a password. - You can add the gateway's Device Access Code. Glade checks it by signing in and keeps it in your Keychain, where no AI ever sees it.
### Little Snitch
- Import a Little Snitch backup on Network, and Glade points out rules that let anything through, duplicates, conflicts, rules for apps you've removed, and ones unused for a year. - **Review with Assistant** explains what to tidy. **Save Cleaned Backup…** writes your backup without the rules it suggested deleting, ready for Little Snitch's own Restore from Backup, which saves your current rules first. The review also names Little Snitch's filters for doing it by hand. - Glade only reads the file you choose. It never touches Little Snitch itself.
### The Assistant remembers
- It follows the conversation, so "and the other one?" or "is it safe to quit that?" is answered in the light of what came before. **New Conversation** starts afresh. - When an answer learns something lasting, such as your internet provider or a problem that keeps coming back, it offers **Remember**. Your notes go with every question after that, and you can change them in **Settings > Assistant**. - **Settings > Protection > Always clear**: name an app you no longer use, and its leftovers and caches are ticked whenever you clean. Leftovers go to the Trash. Personal files, installed apps and anything that can't come back never are, and unattended cleans leave these rules out.
### Command line and AI agents
- `glade network` says where a slowdown is, with the readings behind it. `glade network watch` follows latency second by second and names what was busiest at each spike. `glade network check www.netflix.com` tells a slow service from a slow connection. Also `glade network usage`, `apps`, `router` and `test`, which says how much data it would use before you confirm. - `glade littlesnitch` imports, reviews and writes a cleaned backup; `glade notes` and `glade rules` manage what the Assistant remembers and always clears; `glade ask --continue` follows on from your last question. - Coding agents connected to Glade get the same tools. They see verdicts, numbers and app names, never your network's name, addresses or device names.
